shake preparation rejects omitted states and altered production bytes before drawing

pixelEquivalence.testName: prepared alpha and shared prefixes retain all reference pixels, classes and strict decisions
pixelEquivalence.oldComputationScope: The frozen pre-improvement compositor exists only in the test source as a comparison oracle
comparison: Read old and new reference RGB files and compare every byte for every logical reference
Use every old reference RGB as the completed observation; compare complete class, distance, reference, and visibility results
Compare both the new reference bytes with the unchanged pure classifier and the new streaming file classifier against the frozen old compositor

Include different actual background bytes, different crop, omitted target, foreign target, two-layer order swap, repeated image with same/different phase and distinct PNG bindings with identical bytes
pixelEquivalence.countsMeaning: 413 calculations plus 757 byte-verified reuses belong to all synthetic completed/reference combinations; 153 is the logical reference pixel-comparison count

frameExtraction.comparison: Each selected decoded RGB equals the pre-improvement single-frame seek/extraction result

rejectionCoverage: Missing and extra extraction outputs, including extra output in an empty caption scope
Duplicate, conflicting or reversed global/media frame mapping; zero-length render range
Adjacent selected frame substituted into extraction command while recomputing its canonical hash
Same-count decoded-frame order swap and timestamp shift with recomputed execution digests
Changed alpha/source bindings, missing preparation process, false reference sharing, detached RGB or output artifact chain
Omitted caption, wrong native state/order, stale input/media identity, RGB file mutation, unequal-image tie
limits: Synthetic pixel equality and contract tests do not establish human visual/audio quality or UI acceptance
Per-test temporary PNG/RGB/media fixtures were removed by the test teardown; saved TAP and source remain, and no raw-fixture retention is claimed
This record was assembled from existing successful runs without rerunning the tests
Frame count checks alone do not infer image timestamps; command binding, global/local recipe clocks and old/new decoded-byte comparison provide separate checks
